# os

```go
import "github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/os"
```

Package os \- built\-in os lib VFS implementation.

### Usage

The OS backend interacts directly with the local operating system's file system.

It can be initialized using the backend registry:

```
import(
    "github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend"
    _os "github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/os"
)

func UseFs() error {
    fs := backend.Backend(_os.Scheme)
    // Use fs
    ...
}
```

Or by calling directly:

```
import _os "github.com/c2fo/vfs/v7/backend/os"

func DoSomething() {
    fs := _os.NewFileSystem()

    // Or with a custom temporary directory
    fsWithOpts := _os.NewFileSystem(
        _os.WithTempDir{TempDir: "/path/to/my/temp"},
    )
    ...
}
```

### Options

The OS backend supports the following options for NewFileSystem:

- WithTempDir: Specifies a custom directory path for temporary files used during write operations. If not provided, the backend uses the system temp directory when it's on the same device as the target file, or falls back to the target file's parent directory.

### Read\\\-only files

Reading does not require write access. Read and Seek open the existing file with os.O\_RDONLY \(and never create it\), so files the process cannot write to can be read, seeked and copied from. Writes are staged in a temp file and renamed over the original on Close, and Close only needs the original's name, so replacing a read\-only file requires write permission on its directory rather than on the file itself. \(On Windows the rename is refused while the file carries the read\-only attribute.\)

### See Also

See: https://golang.org/pkg/os/

```go

```

For \`file:///some/path/to/file.txt\`, it would return \`file.txt\`

<a name="File.Path"></a>
### func \(\*File\) Path

```go
func (f *File) Path() string
```

Path returns absolute path, including filename, For \`file:///some/path/to/file.txt\`, it would return \`/some/path/to/file.txt\`

If the directory portion of a file is desired, call

```
someFile.Location().Path()
```

<a name="File.Seek"></a>
### func \(\*File\) Seek

```go
func (f *File) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)
```

Seek implements the io.Seeker interface. It accepts an offset and "whence" where 0 means relative to the origin of the file, 1 means relative to the current offset, and 2 means relative to the end. It returns the new offset and an error, if any.

## type Location

Location implements the vfs.Location interface specific to OS fs.

```go
type Location struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Location.Authority"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) Authority

```go
func (l *Location) Authority() authority.Authority
```

Authority returns the location's authority as a string.

<a name="Location.ChangeDir"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) ChangeDir

```go
func (l *Location) ChangeDir(relativePath string) error
```

ChangeDir takes a relative path, and modifies the underlying Location's path. The caller is modified by this so the only return is any error. For this implementation there are no errors.

Deprecated: Use NewLocation instead:

```
loc, err := loc.NewLocation("../../")
```

<a name="Location.DeleteFile"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) DeleteFile

```go
func (l *Location) DeleteFile(fileName string, opts ...options.DeleteOption) error
```

DeleteFile deletes the file of the given name at the location. This is meant to be a short cut for instantiating a new file and calling delete on that with all the necessary error handling overhead.

<a name="Location.Exists"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) Exists

```go
func (l *Location) Exists() (bool, error)
```

Exists returns true if the location exists, and the calling user has the appropriate permissions. Will receive false without an error if the location simply doesn't exist. Otherwise could receive false and any errors passed back from the OS.

<a name="Location.FileSystem"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) FileSystem

```go
func (l *Location) FileSystem() vfs.FileSystem
```

FileSystem returns a vfs.FileSystem interface of the location's underlying file system.

<a name="Location.List"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) List

```go
func (l *Location) List() ([]string, error)
```

List returns a slice of all files in the top directory of the location.

<a name="Location.ListByPrefix"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) ListByPrefix

```go
func (l *Location) ListByPrefix(prefix string) ([]string, error)
```

ListByPrefix returns a slice of all files starting with "prefix" in the top directory of the location.

<a name="Location.ListByRegex"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) ListByRegex

```go
func (l *Location) ListByRegex(regex *regexp.Regexp) ([]string, error)
```

ListByRegex returns a slice of all files matching the regex in the top directory of the location.

<a name="Location.NewFile"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) NewFile

```go
func (l *Location) NewFile(fileName string, opts ...options.NewFileOption) (vfs.File, error)
```

NewFile uses the properties of the calling location to generate a vfs.File \(backed by an os.File\). A string argument is expected to be a relative path to the location's current path.

<a name="Location.NewLocation"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) NewLocation

```go
func (l *Location) NewLocation(relativePath string) (vfs.Location, error)
```

NewLocation makes a copy of the underlying Location, then modifies its path by calling ChangeDir with the relativePath argument, returning the resulting location. The only possible errors come from the call to ChangeDir.

<a name="Location.Path"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) Path

```go
func (l *Location) Path() string
```

Path returns the location path.

<a name="Location.String"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) String

```go
func (l *Location) String() string
```

String implement fmt.Stringer, returning the location's URI as the default string.

<a name="Location.URI"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) URI

```go
func (l *Location) URI() string
```

URI returns the Location's URI as a string.

<a name="Location.Volume"></a>
### func \(\*Location\) Volume

```go
func (l *Location) Volume() string
```

Volume returns the volume, if any, of the location. Given "C:\\foo\\bar" it returns "C:" on Windows. On other platforms it returns "".

Deprecated: Use Authority instead.

```
authStr := loc.Authority().String()
```

<a name="WithTempDir"></a>
## type WithTempDir

WithTempDir specifies a custom directory for intermediate temporary files used during write operations. This is useful when the system temp directory is on a different device/volume than the target file, which would otherwise cause cross\-device rename errors.

```go
type WithTempDir struct {
    TempDir string
}
```

<a name="WithTempDir.Apply"></a>
### func \(WithTempDir\) Apply

```go
func (o WithTempDir) Apply(fs *FileSystem)
```

Apply applies the temp dir option to the given FileSystem.

### func \(WithTempDir\) NewFileSystemOptionName

```go
func (o WithTempDir) NewFileSystemOptionName() string
```

NewFileSystemOptionName returns the option name.
